claim: DDPM defines the forward process as a fixed Markov chain with closed-form marginal q(x_t|x_0); linear schedule with T=1000, beta_1=1e-4, beta_T=0.02
quote: q(x_{t-1}|x_t, x_0) allows sampling x_t at any arbitrary noise level via closed form given x_0 and the variance schedule

claim: Improved DDPM introduces cosine noise schedule (f(t)=cos^2 formula) to fix aggressive noise addition of linear schedule; offset s=0.008
quote: a linear schedule is not well suited for low resolution images, as samples get too noisy early on in the forward noising process; a cosine schedule avoids such problems

claim: Song et al. unify DDPM and SMLD as discretisations of VP-SDE and VE-SDE respectively; reverse-time SDE depends only on the score function
quote: the reverse-time SDE depends only on the time-dependent gradient field (also known as score) of the perturbed data distribution

claim: Optimal noise schedule shifts toward noisier levels as image resolution increases; input-scaling by factor b is a practical single-parameter resolution fix enabling 1024px generation
quote: the noise scheduling is crucial for the performance, and the optimal one depends on the task (e.g., image sizes)

claim: Common diffusion schedules (linear, cosine) do not enforce zero terminal SNR; this restricts Stable Diffusion to medium brightness and creates training/inference mismatch
quote: Common diffusion noise schedules do not enforce the last timestep to have zero signal-to-noise ratio, creating a discrepancy between training and inference

claim: EDM (Karras 2022) introduces sigma-based continuous-time schedule with rho-polynomial interpolation (sigma_min=0.002, sigma_max=80, rho=7) and lognormal training distribution, achieving FID 1.79 on CIFAR-10
quote: the design space clearly separates the concrete design choices, yielding new state-of-the-art FID of 1.79 for CIFAR-10 with 35 network evaluations per image

claim: Importance sampling of log-SNR is mathematically equivalent to changing the noise schedule; Laplace schedule concentrated near log-SNR=0 achieves FID 7.96 vs cosine 10.85 on ImageNet-256
quote: concentrating sampling probability around log-SNR=0 yields superior training efficiency; Laplace schedule achieves FID 10K of 7.96, a 26.6% improvement over cosine baseline

claim: Sigmoid schedule demonstrates greater stability than cosine for high-resolution images due to smooth transitions avoiding abrupt changes
quote: the sigmoid noise schedule demonstrates greater stability compared to the cosine noise schedule for high-resolution images, mitigating abrupt transitions

claim: Cosine beta schedule formula: ᾱ_t = cos^2(pi/2 * (t/T+s)/(1+s))/cos^2(pi/2*s/(1+s)); s=0.008 offset derived from pixel bin size 1/127.5
quote: the offset value stems from maintaining standard deviation (sqrt(beta_t)) smaller than bin size; with a bin size of 1/127.5, this relationship yields the s=0.008 parameter

claim: Linear schedule applies noise uniformly across all timesteps; for low-resolution images samples get too noisy early in the forward process
quote: Linear applies noise uniformly across timesteps — if a model uses 1,000 timesteps, the noise level might increase linearly from 0% to 100%

claim: Sigmoid schedule provides good balance between computational efficiency and generation quality; cosine results in more stable training and higher-quality outputs
quote: Cosine Schedule often results in more stable training and higher-quality outputs; Sigmoid offers good balance between computational efficiency and generation quality

claim: VE-SDE has no drift term and variance grows geometrically; VP-SDE uses drift -1/2 beta(t) x to maintain bounded variance; SMLD and DDPM are discretisations of these
quote: SMLD represents a discrete implementation of the VE framework; DDPM discretizes the VP SDE

claim: EDM Euler scheduler parameters: sigma_min=0.002, sigma_max=80.0, sigma_data=0.5, rho=7.0; implements Karras et al. 2022 formulation
quote: sigma_min=0.002 (minimum noise magnitude), sigma_max=80.0 (maximum noise magnitude), sigma_data=0.5 (standard deviation of the data distribution), rho=7.0

claim: Resolution-dependent schedule shift: higher-resolution images exhibit greater information redundancy at equivalent noise levels; simply scaling input by b shifts log-SNR without schedule redesign
quote: parameter adjustments can lead to substantial variations in performance; maintain a basic linear schedule and adjust the input scaling factor b based on resolution

claim: WACV 2024: proposes rescaling noise schedule to zero terminal SNR, v-prediction, and sampler fix to eliminate training/inference mismatch
quote: simple changes to rescale the noise schedule to enforce zero terminal SNR and change the sampler to always start from the last timestep ensure the diffusion process is congruent between training and inference

claim: Rectified flow matches DDPM-1000 quality in 5-10 steps; flow matching uses uniform log-SNR distribution equivalent to a specific schedule; 25-step rectified diffusion beats rectified flow on FID and CLIP score
quote: with 1-10 deterministic steps, rectified flow reaches DDPM-1000 fidelity; flow matching models typically adopt a grid that is uniform in log signal-noise ratio space
